title: Kinsing_Rootkit_Investigation_6f3
description: Investigate a compromised system to identify the Kinsing rootkit's presence and determine the extent of the compromise.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Kinsing rootkit is a sophisticated malware family targeting Linux systems. It exploits vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access, maintains persistence through various mechanisms, and establishes command-and-control (C2) communication channels. Your task is to investigate a compromised system, identify the rootkit's presence, and determine the extent of the compromise.

levels.title: Identify Evidence of Shared Library Injection
levels.content: Investigate the victim host to determine if any unauthorized shared libraries have been loaded into system processes. Look for indicators of code injection that could be associated with the Kinsing rootkit. The sandbox contains evidence of the Kinsing rootkit's shared library injection in the form of the file /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsysmon.so.1.
levels.solution: Check the loaded libraries for each process and look for any suspicious or unauthorized entries. The hidden flag is the identifier of the shared library used for injection.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the loaded libraries for each process and look for any suspicious or unauthorized entries.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for hidden files or directories that may have been created or modified by the Kinsing rootkit.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use commands like lsof or ldd to inspect process libraries and identify any unauthorized entries.

levels.title: Determine Modified System-Wide Preload Configuration
levels.content: Examine the system-wide preload configuration to see if it has been altered to load unauthorized shared libraries. This could indicate a persistence mechanism used by the Kinsing rootkit. The sandbox contains evidence of the Kinsing rootkit's modified system-wide preload configuration in the form of the file /etc/ld.so.preload.
levels.solution: Inspect the preload configuration file and check for any unusual or unauthorized entries. The hidden flag is the identifier of the preload configuration used for unauthorized code execution.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Inspect the preload configuration file and check for any unusual or unauthorized entries.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for hidden files or directories that may have been created or modified by the Kinsing rootkit.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use commands like cat or less to examine the contents of the preload configuration file.

levels.title: Locate Hidden Files or Directories
levels.content: Search the victim host for any hidden files or directories that may have been created or modified by the Kinsing rootkit. These artifacts could provide valuable insights into the rootkit's behavior and persistence mechanisms. The sandbox contains evidence of the Kinsing rootkit's hidden files or directories in the form of the file /etc/.kit_conf/config.
levels.solution: Use forensic techniques to uncover hidden filesystem artifacts that are not visible through standard system utilities. The hidden flag is the identifier of the hidden artifact.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use forensic techniques to uncover hidden filesystem artifacts that are not visible through standard system utilities.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for hidden files or directories that may have been created or modified by the Kinsing rootkit.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use commands like find or ls with appropriate options to reveal hidden files and directories.
